name: Shalmaneser
title: King of Assyria who besieged Samaria
summary: Shalmaneser V was king of Assyria who imposed tribute on Hoshea, the last king of Israel, and later besieged Samaria when Hoshea rebelled. His siege of Samaria led to the fall of the northern kingdom and the exile of the ten tribes, marking the end of Israel's northern kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Hoshea submits to Shalmaneser
keyEvents.description: Hoshea, king of Israel, became a vassal of Shalmaneser and paid tribute to him.

keyEvents.title: Hoshea's rebellion uncovered
keyEvents.description: Shalmaneser discovered that Hoshea had conspired with Egypt and stopped paying tribute, which led to Hoshea being imprisoned.

keyEvents.title: The siege of Samaria begins
keyEvents.description: Shalmaneser marched against the entire land and besieged Samaria for three years as punishment for Hoshea's rebellion.

keyEvents.title: The Fall of Samaria and the Exile of Israel
keyEvents.description: After a three-year siege, Samaria fell, and the Israelites were taken captive to Assyria and settled in various cities and regions.

keyEvents.title: The Cause of Israel's Fall
keyEvents.description: The Bible explains that the fall of Samaria was due to Israel's sin against the Lord, their idolatry, and disobedience to the covenant.
